content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs against the disclosure and the affirmative USER passages in the conversation.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 20 claims (device 1-10, system 11-15, method 16-20) were traced limitation by limitation to the disclosure: rigid base with first/second side, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter loop/skirt of plastic, metal, PTFE or a combination, non-sealing restriction of airflow with continuous ingress beneath the perimeter, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, a holding force replacing operator downforce, an all-rigid motor-to-tile path with no rubber or foam, free sliding across areas of the tile, guiding handles, and a rope/wire/cable pulling element giving decoupled position-versus-hold control. Claim 10's stirring elements and the Field's "autonomously moving" clause trace to the affirmative USER passage adding autonomous mode ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"); the many "resume/rebuild/tighten the Field" USER turns were treated as operational only and not as disclosure. All 17 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each has one consistent meaning across the numeral table, the detailed description, the claims and the briefs, each appears on at least one sheet, and no numeral is defined in a brief without a description antecedent. All six figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings were checked for structure beyond the sources: the slab/band/block outlines, rectangular plan form, frame width, hatching, the schematic gap through the slab beneath the air-extraction housing, the flat lower end of the column in FIG. 4, the pulling-element meeting place in FIG. 5, and the number, form and drawn position of the stirring elements in FIG. 6 are all marked as depiction conventions confined to the briefs, and none of them verbalizes taper, angle, runout, deeper-end, contact-topology or material relationships absent from the sources. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same repeated designation in the FIG. 3 source-view brief, the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 resulting-view briefs, the Brief Description, and the detailed description. Title, cross-reference and government-support sections match the filing brief; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section body, and no section heading is duplicated inside a body. One verified internal inconsistency was found and is reported: the FIG. 3 brief's disclaimer denying any distribution of contact and clearance around the perimeter contradicts the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs and the Brief Description, which locate line 2-2 where the perimeter member bears and line 4-4 where the clearance is present. No unsupported technical assertion was found in the claims, description, abstract or briefs.

findings.title: FIG. 3 brief denies the contact/clearance distribution that FIG. 2, FIG. 4 and the Brief Description both depict and recite
findings.detail: The FIG. 3 brief instructs that the two section lines assert no distribution of contact and clearance around the perimeter member. But the same two lines are the source views for FIG. 2 and FIG. 4, and those briefs and the filed Brief Description expressly assign one line to a bearing position and the other to a clearance position: FIG. 2 is cut 'where the perimeter member bears on it' with 'each leg rests on the band' and 'the clearance appears only in FIG. 4', while FIG. 4 is cut 'where the clearance is present'. As drawn, FIG. 3 therefore does indicate one circumferential position with rigid contact and another with clearance, so the disclaimer contradicts the sheets it points to. The partial-contact/partial-clearance condition itself is source-supported ('the rigid perimeter is not intended to form a complete airtight seal... Instead, it restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile'), and the description states the clearance remains 'along at least part of the perimeter member 24'; the overreaching clause in the FIG. 3 brief is the defective element, not the depiction. The remaining hedge that the specific angular position drawn is a placement convention is accurate and may stand.
findings.evidence: FIG-3 brief: 'Their drawn positions, including the angular position at which each crosses the ring, are a placement convention for this sheet only, no distribution of contact and clearance around the perimeter member 24 being asserted.' FIG-2 brief View: 'Vertical section taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 3, through the vibration device of FIG. 1 and the covering element 36 beneath it, where the perimeter member bears on it... The vibration motor and the handle are omitted; the clearance appears only in FIG. 4.' FIG-4 brief View: 'Enlarged fragmentary section taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3, through the lower end of the perimeter member where the clearance is present.' draft/07-drawings.md: 'FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3, at a place along the perimeter member where the clearance is present...'
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3-BOTTOM-PLAN-VIEW-OF-THE-VIBRATION-DEVICE.md, replace the sentence 'Their drawn positions, including the angular position at which each crosses the ring, are a placement convention for this sheet only, no distribution of contact and clearance around the perimeter member 24 being asserted.' with 'Their drawn positions, including the angular position at which each crosses the ring, are a placement convention for this sheet only.' Make no change to the FIG. 2 or FIG. 4 briefs, to draft/07-drawings.md, or to any claim, numeral definition or description passage.
